Incident evidence from a live occurrence, carried here from the #2384 session. Recording it on this task rather than filing a duplicate — a just-filed task (#2653) describing this same defect was archived once the sibling-overlap advisory surfaced #2560 and #2508.

## What happened

Task #2384 (`kind: infra`, `wf-fix`) reached Step 10d on 2026-08-31 with every gate green:

- Round-5 code review: Claude PASS (`epm:code-review` event v6) AND Codex twin PASS (`epm:code-review-codex` event v5, `CONCERN:: none`) — a PASS+PASS round with no reconciler.
- Concerns ledger empty.
- Step 9c selected set on the exact HEAD: 9292 passed, 12 skipped, 0 failed, rc=0.

The pre-push workflow-lint gate then returned `block` and the merge parked at `epm:merge-failed v1`. The branch and PR #2128 are prepared and the merge retries idempotently, but the deliverable is not on `main`.

## The blocking line, in full

The diff between the normalized baseline and gated failure-line sets was exactly ONE line:

```
workflow_lint: note: --check-no-unannotated-gcp-pin-guidance scanned 1402 file(s), 0 WARN(s)
```

Baseline read `1401`. The payload adds `scripts/check_cited_body_currency.py`, which legitimately enters that check's scan cone. So the count moved by one, and the count is the whole delta.

## Why it produced a block rather than a harmless diff

Every substantive signal the gate exists to read was clean:

- `lint-owndiff` EMPTY — no lint error attributable to the payload.
- `tg-new*` EMPTY — no new test failure.
- Baseline and gated BOTH `FAIL (23)`, sharing 21 identical pre-existing error identities (bare-Hub-call / import-guard / splitlines offenders in `scripts/issue2643_*` and `scripts/issue779_ctxansviz_*`).
- The 3 failed test nodes are byte-identical to the merge-base baseline.

The red baseline is what converts the false NEW line into a verdict: with `GATED_RC != 0` from unrelated pre-existing trunk red, the verdict writes `block`. That trunk-red condition is separately owned by #2649 (running), #2648, and #2586, so this defect and that one compound — either one alone would have let the merge through.

## Note on scope, if useful to whoever takes this

The gate's own FAIL-summary drop rationale already names this exact count-instability class and handles it for `FAIL (N)` lines; the `note:` lines were missed. At least two checks emit them: `--check-no-unannotated-gcp-pin-guidance` and `--check-lane-order-adjective` (`scanned N file(s)`).

Both executable blocks need the change — the form (i)/(ii) workload and the form (iii) surgical block. A fix to one leaves the other reachable.

Blanking the `scanned [0-9]+ file\(s\)` count tokens, the way `:<line>:` numbers are already blanked, is more conservative than dropping `note:` lines wholesale: it keeps a genuinely new `note:` line visible when it appears for some reason other than a count shift.

## Downstream

#2384's Step 10d re-enters idempotently once this lands (or once the trunk red clears): branch `issue-2384` is pushed, PR #2128 is open, and the guards re-run from scratch. No work needs redoing there.
